Masking may store invalid depths/points as infinity; apply the valid mask before geometry processing.

license.code: MIT; third-party dependencies retain their own terms

input.frames: One RGB perspective image or one complete ERP panorama
input.projection: Perspective directly; complete ERP through the official ERP-to-six-face 95-degree cubemap pipeline
input.intrinsics: Perspective: optional fov_x, otherwise recovered. ERP: fixed virtual intrinsics and rotations are generated by projection, not measured real-camera pose.
input.resolution: Panorama benchmark: six 518x518 faces reprojected to a 512x1024 ERP depth map; public code can project to other target dimensions
input.extrinsics: No measured camera extrinsics; ERP uses known virtual cubemap rotations around one shared center

input.synchronization: Single-image inference; six cubemap faces are derived from the same ERP, not a temporal sequence

output.primary: Metric pinhole Z-depth or panoramic radial range, metric 3D point maps, normals and validity mask

output.normal: Predicted surface normals; panorama geometry is represented on cubemap faces before ERP fusion

output.camera_parameters: Perspective normalized K with centered principal point; no estimated real-camera extrinsics

depth_convention: Perspective infer(): depth_from_pts=points[...,2], followed by learned metric_scale, so depth is optical-axis Z. Official ERP evaluator multiplies pts3d by metric_scale, computes norm(points), and blends the six range maps back to ERP. Cubemap Z and panoramic range must not be interchanged.
scale: Learned metric scale; one shared scale across panorama faces. Scale-/affine-invariant evaluations additionally align predictions to GT and are separate from raw metric performance.
pose_output: No estimated camera pose or trajectory; virtual cubemap poses are known projection conditions
runtime: Paper reports 531 ms for a 1024x2048 ERP on A100 versus DAP 427 ms; no local runtime or memory measurement. Protocol-specific timings are not end-to-end SLAM benchmarks.
innovation: Canonicalizes ERP to overlapping perspective patches, conditions a shared Transformer on virtual cameras, and trains correspondence consistency across overlaps with a shared metric-scale head.
summary_zh: 统一针孔与完整 ERP 的单图公制几何模型；全景内部转为六个重叠透视面，利用虚拟相机条件与对应一致性约束，输出径向距离和点图。
engineering_notes: This record is the 2026 PolyU perspective/panorama model, not the unrelated 2025 diffusion paper named DepthMaster.
The official repository reports NeurIPS 2026 acceptance in September 2026; an archival proceedings record was not independently verified.

Full ERP is an official external input. Internally, six overlapping 95-degree perspective faces share virtual camera conditioning and a learned global scale. These virtual faces are not a physical multi-camera rig.

Table 1 on PDF page 7 reports metric AbsRel below DAP on Stanford2D3D (7.73 vs 10.89), Matterport3D (9.49 vs 17.78) and PanoSUNCG (4.54 vs 6.71), with mean 7.25 vs 11.79, using the table display values. These are author-reported indoor-benchmark results, not an independently reproduced universal ranking.

For metric reproduction, set evaluation.metric_depth_eval=true: the released panorama config defaults to scale/affine-aligned evaluation. Follow eval_panorama/eval.py or the README forward-plus-metric_scale path; the convenience infer_panorama() wrapper does not itself apply metric_scale.
No verified raw fisheye interface or camera trajectory output. Single-image geometry does not establish temporal consistency or SLAM accuracy.
environment: Official README tested Linux, Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.4.0 and CUDA 12.1; pin utils3d to commit 3fab839f0be9931dac7c8488eb0e1600c236e183. No local inference or compatibility test.

title: OmniPoint: Universal Monocular Metric Pointcloud from Any Camera
venue: ECCV 2026 (official project and author pages); arXiv 2609.09394

license.code: Unknown: no author-linked public inference implementation verified.
license.weights: Unknown: no author-linked public checkpoint or checkpoint license verified.

input.frames: One RGB image; optional camera calibration and/or aligned sparse depth.
input.projection: Pinhole perspective, raw fisheye and complete equirectangular panorama are explicitly documented input types; not merely virtual pinhole crops at inference.
input.intrinsics: Optional camera model/calibration is converted to a per-pixel ray map. RGB-only inference predicts rays without measured intrinsics.
input.resolution: Exact public inference resize, tensor shape and preprocessing are unverified because no author-linked implementation was located.
input.extrinsics: Not required for image-only inference; a sparse-depth sensor must be externally aligned to the image.
input.gravity: No measured gravity input documented.
input.synchronization: Single-image prediction. Sparse depth must correspond to the same image geometry; sensor calibration and synchronization are external integration requirements.
input.sparse_depth: Optional LiDAR/SfM sparse condition; normalized by its valid-value mean, Gaussian-smoothed, and supplied with a validity mask. Metric sparse conditions allow post-alignment of the prediction.

output.primary: Dense metric camera-centered point map, predicted unit rays, radial distance, global metric scale and sky-region mask.
output.point_map: P = s * d * r, where r is a unit ray, d the predicted radial distance and s a learned global metric scale.
output.normal: Normal consistency is a training loss; no separate normal-output head documented.
output.confidence: Sky-region masking head, not a calibrated depth-uncertainty output.
output.camera_parameters: Per-pixel ray field; optional calibrated rays condition the model. No public K recovery API or extrinsic/trajectory output verified.

depth_convention: The central representation is Euclidean radial distance along unit camera rays. Metric points are s*d*r and metric range is norm(P)=s*d. This is not inherently pinhole Z-depth; a point-map Z component is coordinate-axis dependent and does not remain a positive full-panorama depth. Serialized output conventions remain unverified without released source.
scale: RGB-only prediction uses a learned global metric scale. Optional metric sparse depth supplies external scale through post-alignment; sparse-conditioned results must not be reported as image-only monocular performance.
pose_output: No camera pose, trajectory, VO/VIO state or loop-closure output documented.
runtime: No local inference timing or peak-memory measurement. Reported 72 A100 GPUs describe training, not inference requirements.
innovation: Separates camera rays from radial scene structure, combines bidirectional 3D camera augmentation with input-state embeddings and Gaussian-smoothed geometric conditions.
summary_zh: 统一针孔、原始鱼眼和完整 ERP 的单图公制点图模型，以射线与径向距离解耦相机和场景；可选内参与稀疏深度，需区分纯图像与条件输入结果。
engineering_notes: Official project and author pages identify ECCV 2026; a publisher chapter DOI was not independently verified.
Camera support is paper-documented, not locally reproduced: the official project links paper/poster/BibTeX but no verified public inference code or checkpoint as of 2026-10-20.
The panoramic baseline in Table 2 is DA-squared / Depth Anything in Any Direction, not DAP / Depth Any Panoramas. No direct DAP comparison was found in the reviewed official paper/project.
Table 2 reports relative geometry on Stanford2D3D-S and PanoSUNCG; it does not establish metric panoramic superiority over DAP.
Table 3 separates image-only, intrinsics-conditioned and sparse-depth-conditioned metric evaluations on six pinhole datasets. Stronger conditioned rows cannot be assigned to image-only inference.
A normal consistency training loss does not prove an independent normal prediction output; sky masking is not calibrated geometric confidence.
Single-image point maps do not establish temporal consistency, real camera motion or SLAM accuracy.
environment: Paper architecture: DINOv2 ViT-L backbone and DPT prediction heads. Public installable inference dependencies, hardware support and exact version requirements are unverified.
reproduction_status: Official paper/project reviewed and real paper figure inspected; no model inference performed and no code/checkpoint release verified.

title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields

license.weights: Unknown: official model/checkpoint release is TBD.

input.frames: One RGB image from a central camera; no camera-type label or measured camera calibration.
input.projection: Complete ERP, pinhole and fisheye inputs are explicitly evaluated. A separate held-out Nayar catadioptric case is annular, not another ERP representation.
input.intrinsics: No intrinsics or distortion parameters required by the described inference; the model predicts a per-pixel unit ray field.
input.resolution: Paper training images range from 896x1792 ERP to 512x512 lens crops, with an 8192-token cap. Released inference resize/API remains unavailable.
input.extrinsics: Not required; one shared central viewpoint is assumed.
input.gravity: No measured gravity input; panoramic training sampling keeps source horizons gravity-aligned.
input.synchronization: One image, no temporal synchronization input.

output.primary: Dense camera-frame 3D point map, unit rays and positive radial distances, recovered up to one global scale.
output.point_map: P(u)=rho(u)*d(u); d is a unit camera ray and rho is its radial distance.
output.confidence: No calibrated uncertainty or confidence-output head documented.
output.camera_parameters: Composite dense ray field; no verified public intrinsics-parameter API or camera extrinsics output.

depth_convention: rho is positive Euclidean distance along a unit ray, not optical-axis Z. P=rho*d. The point map and range retain global scale ambiguity; serialized outputs are unverified without released code.
scale: Up-to-scale geometry. All reported reconstruction methods use per-image median scale alignment; the paper does not establish absolute metric reconstruction.
pose_output: No camera pose, trajectory or SLAM state output documented.
runtime: No comparable local inference timing or peak-memory measurement. Eight A40 GPUs describe training, not an inference requirement.
innovation: Composes a monotone radial camera base with spherical-harmonic and free-form residual rotations, then combines the ray field with a DPT radial-distance prediction.
summary_zh: 以单调径向基底、球谐残差和自由场残差组合相机射线，统一针孔、鱼眼和完整 ERP 的单图相对三维点图；不需要相机类型或内参，但不恢复绝对米制尺度。
engineering_notes: First submitted 2026-10-22; this is a new paper in the current weekly window, not a backfilled older model.
The official project explicitly says code and models are TBD; its Code, Demo and Checkpoint buttons point to the arXiv page rather than released artifacts as checked on 2026-10-26.
Paper Sec. 4.3 and Table 2 align each method per image by the ratio of ground-truth and predicted median radial distance. Scale-aligned results must not be labeled absolute metric accuracy.
The central-camera assumption requires rays to share a viewpoint. A noncentral stitched rig is not validated merely by the any-camera title.
Training uses 2D3DS and 360Loc source panoramas plus sampled lens views. Held-out GoPro/catadioptric geometry and unseen PanoCity/CO3Dv2 tests have different scopes.
Comparisons include UniK3D and DA3 under the author protocol; no direct DAP comparison was found in the reviewed paper/project. Single-image geometry does not provide a continuous trajectory.
environment: Paper describes DINOv2 ViT-L/14 and a DPT distance head; encoder bfloat16 and heads/losses full precision. Public installable code, package versions and supported inference platforms remain TBD.
reproduction_status: Original paper/project reviewed and original method figure visually checked; no inference performed.
